subject: EdgeData RFP — Misuse monitoring & reporting clarifications
messages:
From: Procurement <procurement@edgedata.com>

Cc: tim.cho@edgedata.com

Subject: EdgeData RFP — Misuse Monitoring & Reporting Clarifications

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the RFP — we've reviewed Redwood's submission at a high level and have a few follow-ups specifically focused on misuse monitoring, policy controls, and reporting:

1) Retention & access: What is the default retention period for telemetry and content logs used for misuse detection? Can this be configured per-tenant and for how long (max retention and export options)? Who can access full-text logs?
2) Detection coverage: Which signals are evaluated (model output, user input, streaming deltas, contextual metadata, KV cache)? Are there pre-built classifiers for harassment, sexual content, fraud, and regulatory misuse?
3) Real-time alerting: What are the SLA/latency expectations for an alert to be generated from receipt to customer notification? Is there support for severity tiers and dedup windows?
4) False positives / escalation: How are FP rates surfaced and what customer controls exist for escalating or suppressing recurring false positives?
5) Data export & integration: Can alerts and raw events be pushed to customer SIEMs (Splunk/Datadog/Arcsight) or S3? What formats and auth methods are supported?
6) Compliance & evidence: Is there an audit trail we can request for incidents, and what attestation (SOC2, ISO) do you provide?

We attached our RFP bundle for reference (edgedata_rfp_20261101.pdf). The security and procurement teams would appreciate a consolidated technical appendix with explicit answers and any matrices you use for mapping detectors to categories.

Can you respond with a single consolidated reply and any attachments by EOD 11/14 PST so we can review ahead of procurement?

Thanks —
Sarah Liu
Head of Procurement, EdgeData Analytics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EdgeData RFP — Misuse Monitoring & Reporting Clarifications

Hi Sarah — thank you for the clear list. Attaching a consolidated response and a detection matrix that maps our detectors to the misuse categories you listed. High-level answers below and the technical appendix attached.

Quick summary (details in attached PDF and matrix):
- Default retention: 90 days for telemetry and analysis traces; configurable per-tenant up to 365 days with an export/archival path. Full-text logs are only available to authorized security/admin roles and require audit approval for export.
- Signals: We evaluate user input, model outputs, streaming token deltas, request metadata (IP, region), and runtime policy hits. We do not persist raw KV cache contents; only structured cache miss/hit metrics are logged.
- Detectors: Rule-based filters + ML ensemble classifiers covering harassment, hate, sexual content, phishing/fraud indicators, regulatory categories (e.g., PII exfiltration patterns). See matrix for mapping and typical precision/recall bands.
- Alerts & SLA: Near-real-time detection with a typical alert generation latency under 1s for streaming matches; customer notification via webhook/SIEM within configurable windows (immediate, 5m aggregate, hourly digest). Severity tiers (P0–P3) and deduplication windows supported.
- False positives: We provide a reviewer workflow for customer feedback; recurring FPs can be suppressed at rule or classifier level. We surface FP metrics on the Console and support export to CSV.
- Integrations & exports: Alerts/events via HTTPS webhooks, AWS Kinesis, S3 delivery (parquet/csv), and syslog for SIEMs. Auth: mTLS and signed tokens.
- Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; audit logs and incident evidence bundles available upon request under an NDA.

I've attached: EdgeData_RFI_Response_20261114.pdf, misuse_monitoring_matrix.xlsx and included a compact telemetry schema. Ben and Rishi are looped for any additional technical clarifications.

Best,
So˜ojin Lee

Ben / team — adding the technical detail to drop straight into the appendix (pasted and summarized here). I also attached the telemetry schema file (redwood_telemetry_schema.md) to the consolidated RFI package.

Telemetry & log schema (summary):
- Event types: REQUEST, RESPONSE, POLICY_HIT, ALERT, AGGREGATE_METRIC, MODEL_INFERENCE_TRACE.
- Core fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, tenant_id, request_id, model_version, seq_len, prompt_truncated (bool), tokens_generated, detector_ids, policy_matches (list), hashed_user_id (one-way salted hash), client_ip (redacted at customer option), region, latency_ms.
- Content logging: default behavior is to NOT persist full request/response text for standard tenants; full-text capture is opt-in for troubleshooting under strict access controls (audited, short retention). We persist derived features and detectors' token indices, offsets, and redaction masks.
- KV cache: only meta metrics (hit_rate, miss_rate) logged; we deliberately avoid storing cache contents.

Detection & pipeline:
- Hybrid detectors: first-pass deterministic rules (regexes, blocklists) -> ML ensemble classifiers (contextual embeddings + sequence-aware model) -> anomaly detector for emergent risk patterns.
- Thresholding & dedupe: alerts are generated per request but deduped across a configurable rolling window (default 10 minutes) to reduce alert fatigue. Customers can tune severity thresholds per category.
- Alert enrichment: each alert includes reproducible detector context, scoring, top contributing tokens, and suggested mitigation actions (rate-limit, block, human review).

Integrations & exports:
- Live: webhooks (json with HMAC signing), syslog, Kinesis.
- Bulk: S3 export (parquet preferred) or secure Drive link for evidence bundles. Exports include redaction flags and field-level encryption metadata.

Retention & access:
- Defaults: Telemetry 90 days; alert evidence bundle 180 days.
- Config: tenant-admins can request retention increase to 365 days under contract; exports and long-term archival delegated to customer S3.
- Access control: RBAC on Console, API keys for programmatic exports, and a documented audit workflow for full-text access requests (requires signed request and logs an audit event).

Privacy & compliance:
- PII handling: automatic PII detection with optional on-write redaction; we support token-level masking and hashing.
- Attestations: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we also provide periodic penetration-test summaries.

Playbooks & FP handling:
- Customers can register suppression rules by detector_id. We provide a reviewer UI for marking outcomes (TP/FP/NA) which retrains adaptive thresholds for that tenant. For customer escalations, we open an incident in our SecOps hub and provide an evidence bundle and root-cause analysis within SLA windows.

If you want, I can turn this into a 1–2 page appendix with examples and sample API payloads.

—Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
